title.note: Game title stays in English (glossary keep; the guide keeps game titles).

hud.reel.note: 'sveive inn' is the Norwegian angling verb for reeling in. 9 chars vs the estimated 8; it can wrap at the space on a round button. Shortest fallback: 'Sveiv' (5). Same verb as the pass Autosveiv.

hud.bait_left.note: Label form. 'agn' also has an invariant plural, so it reads right for 0, 1 and more.

catch.success.note: Restructured as 'New catch: ...' so no article or adjective has to agree with the inserted fish name or rarity (the guide's egg.hatched pattern).

catch.escaped.note: 'Fisken' (the fish) instead of a bare 'Den', since the toast has no antecedent.

catch.new_record.note: Developer: {weight} arrives as '12.4'; Norwegian writes a decimal comma ('12,4'), so format it by LocaleId.

fish.lantern_eel.note: Closed compound lanterne + ål (eel); keeps the glowing-lantern idea and the echo of the title.

rarity.mythic.note: Tier above Legendarisk. An -isk adjective does not change in the neuter, so the tag never has to agree with a fish.

shop.rods.note: 12 chars vs the estimated 10. Bare 'Stenger' would also read as the verb 'closes' on a shop tab, so the full compound is the shortest clear word. It cannot wrap; check at phone size.

shop.equip.note: 'Use', paired with the state label 'I bruk' (In use); avoids a participle that would have to agree with fiskestang.

shop.equipped.note: 'In use' as the context allows; the matching button is 'Bruk'.

pass.auto_reel.note: Built from 'sveive inn' (hud.reel) with the closed prefix auto- (as in autolagring). The pass's Creator Hub store name should match.
pass.auto_reel.blind_remark: coined compound, literally 'auto-crank'; understandable next to 'reel in'

pass.lucky_bait.text: Lykkeagn dobler sjansen din for sjeldne fisker!
pass.lucky_bait.note: Lykkeagn = lykke (luck) + agn (bait), like the guide's Lykkedrikk. Plural 'sjeldne fisker' because singular 'sjelden fisk' can also read as 'rarely fish'.

sell.done.note: 'fisk' stays uninflected after a number in fishing talk ('fikk 12 fisk'), so it is right for 1 and for 12. Coins as a label with '+' because '{coins} mynter' breaks at 1.

sell.prompt.note: 'Trykk på E for å selge' (22) is over the 21 budget; the guide accepts the shorter 'Trykk E'.

ascend.button.note: 'stige opp' = rise up a level. No Norwegian Roblox standard exists for prestige; avoided 'Oppstigning' (religious or mountaineering) and English 'Ascend', which kids may not know.
ascend.button.blind_remark: literally 'rise up' or 'climb up'; a bit lofty, could read as physically going up

ascend.confirm.text: Vil du stige opp nå? Du starter på nytt, men fanger sjeldne fisker {bonus} % oftere.
ascend.confirm.note: Same verb as ascend.button. Percent with a space (CLDR). 'sjeldne fisker' because 'fanger sjelden fisk' would read as 'rarely catch fish'.

weather.storm.text: En storm er på vei! Sjeldne fisker biter nå.
weather.storm.note: 'biter' is the angling sense (take the bait); 'nå' carries the English progressive 'are biting'.
weather.storm.blind_remark: says the storm is approaching, not that it is already here

quest.catch_n.note: Moonlit Bay -> Månelysbukten (månelys = moonlight, bukt = bay; -en form per the guide). 'fisk' uninflected after a number, as in sell.done, so n = 1 and n = 10 both read right. 'i' is the natural preposition for fishing in a bay.

friends.boost.note: 'lykke' is the luck stat, the same word as in Lykkeagn; the more casual 'flaks' is the alternative if 'lykke' reads too much like happiness. Percent with a space (CLDR).

trade.sent.note: Formed like 'venneforespørsel' (friend request); 'bytte' is the guide's trade word.

trade.accept.review_reason: 'byttet' also means prey or catch, an easy misreading in a fishing game; 'bytteforespørselen' names the same request as trade.sent (30/33).

codes.redeemed.text: Koden er løst inn! Kos deg med belønningen.
codes.redeemed.note: 'løse inn' is Roblox's own Norwegian verb for redeeming; 'Kos deg med' is the idiomatic 'Enjoy'.

afk.kicked.text: Du var inaktiv for lenge, så fiskingen stoppet.
afk.kicked.note: 'the fishing stopped' rather than 'du sluttet å fiske', which would sound like the player chose to quit.

event.ends.note: 'om' for a point ahead. Developer: {time} arrives as '2d 4h'; Norwegian writes '2 d 4 t' (CLDR short form), so format durations by LocaleId.

daily.streak.text: {day}. dag på rad! Kom tilbake i morgen for flere belønninger.
daily.streak.note: '{day}. dag på rad' = 'day N in a row' with the Norwegian digit-plus-period ordinal, correct for every value. terms.json renders streak as 'rekke' for noun uses; here 'på rad' is the idiom. 'for more' made explicit as 'flere belønninger' (more rewards).

tip.night.text: Tips: Noen fisker biter bare om natten.
tip.night.note: 'Tips:' is the Norwegian label; capital after the colon because a full sentence follows.

group.join.text: Bli med i gruppen og få 50 gratis agn!
group.join.note: 'gruppe' as the guide advises (Roblox's English UI now says Communities). 'agn' is invariant, so '50 gratis agn' is correct.

leaderboard.biggest.note: Usual Norwegian fishing-contest wording; 'fangst' is the catch (noun).
